quests.question: In this context, what part of speech is 'attached'?
quests.sentence: Hi team, please review the attached draft before Thursday's call, and let me know if you spot any errors.
quests.hint: This word, though it comes from a verb, describes the condition of the draft. What kind of draft should the team review?
quests.explanation: 'Attached' functions as an adjective here, modifying 'draft' and describing that it was included with the email.
quests.grammarRule: Participial adjective modifying a noun

quests.question: In that same sentence, what part of speech is 'if'?
quests.sentence: Hi team, please review the attached draft before Thursday's call, and let me know if you spot any errors.
quests.hint: This word introduces a condition. Under what condition should the reader let the sender know?
quests.explanation: 'If' is a subordinating conjunction here, introducing the condition under which the reader should reply — spotting any errors.
quests.grammarRule: Subordinating conjunction introducing a conditional clause

quests.question: Which grammatical category fits 'errors' in that same sentence?
quests.sentence: Hi team, please review the attached draft before Thursday's call, and let me know if you spot any errors.
quests.hint: Set aside what you know about this word in general. What might the reader spot in the draft?
quests.explanation: 'Errors' is a noun here, naming the mistakes the reader might find — it functions as the direct object of 'spot'.
quests.grammarRule: Common noun functioning as a direct object

quests.question: What grammatical job does 'Running' do in this text exchange?
quests.sentence: "Running 10 min late, traffic's terrible!" "No worries, we haven't started yet."
quests.hint: In casual texting, the subject 'I'm' is often dropped. What is the sender doing right now, in an ongoing sense?
quests.explanation: 'Running' functions as part of the verb here — short for 'I'm running' — describing the sender's ongoing lateness, even though the subject and 'is' are left out in this casual text message.
quests.grammarRule: Verb in the present progressive tense (subject omitted)

quests.question: Which part of speech is 'terrible' as it is used here?
quests.sentence: "Running 10 min late, traffic's terrible!" "No worries, we haven't started yet."
quests.hint: Think about the job it performs here. What quality does 'terrible' give the traffic?
quests.explanation: 'Terrible' is an adjective here, describing the traffic's condition, following the linking verb 'is' (shortened to 's).
quests.grammarRule: Predicate adjective after a linking verb

quests.question: Identify the part of speech of 'worries' in this context.
quests.sentence: "Running 10 min late, traffic's terrible!" "No worries, we haven't started yet."
quests.hint: Think about the job it performs here. What does the reply say there's none of?
quests.explanation: 'Worries' is a noun here, naming the concerns the second speaker says are unnecessary — it functions as the object in the phrase 'no worries'.
quests.grammarRule: Common noun functioning as an object

quests.question: What part of speech is 'Due to' in this notice?
quests.sentence: Due to scheduled maintenance, the elevator will be out of service from 9 AM until noon; please use the stairs during this time.
quests.hint: This expression introduces a reason at the start of the notice. What caused the elevator to go out of service?
quests.explanation: 'Due to' functions as a compound preposition here, introducing the reason for the elevator being out of service.
quests.grammarRule: Compound preposition introducing a reason phrase

quests.question: Staying with that notice, which category describes 'until'?
quests.sentence: Due to scheduled maintenance, the elevator will be out of service from 9 AM until noon; please use the stairs during this time.
quests.hint: This word is followed by a simple time word, not a clause. What time does the out-of-service period end?
quests.explanation: 'Until' is a preposition here, introducing the time word 'noon' rather than a full clause.
quests.grammarRule: Preposition introducing an ending point in time

quests.question: Back in that same notice, what kind of word is 'please'?
quests.sentence: Due to scheduled maintenance, the elevator will be out of service from 9 AM until noon; please use the stairs during this time.
quests.hint: This word softens a command without naming an action itself. What effect does 'please' have on the instruction?
quests.explanation: 'Please' functions as an adverb here, softening the request to use the stairs — it makes the instruction sound more polite without changing its meaning.
quests.grammarRule: Adverb softening a command

quests.question: How is 'assembling' functioning in this sentence?
quests.sentence: Before assembling the shelf, make sure all screws are sorted, since missing pieces can delay the process significantly.
quests.hint: This '-ing' word names an activity and follows the preposition 'Before.' What should happen before the shelf is put together?
quests.explanation: 'Assembling' is a gerund here, functioning as the object of the preposition 'Before' — it names the task that comes after checking the screws.
quests.grammarRule: Gerund functioning as the object of a preposition

quests.question: Now consider 'since' in that same sentence. What part of speech is it?
quests.sentence: Before assembling the shelf, make sure all screws are sorted, since missing pieces can delay the process significantly.
quests.hint: This word introduces a reason for sorting the screws first. Why is it important to sort the screws?
quests.explanation: 'Since' functions as a subordinating conjunction here, meaning 'because' — it introduces the reason missing pieces could cause delays.
quests.grammarRule: Subordinating conjunction introducing a reason clause

quests.question: And in that same sentence, what part of speech is 'significantly'?
quests.sentence: Before assembling the shelf, make sure all screws are sorted, since missing pieces can delay the process significantly.
quests.hint: Ask how it connects to the words near it. How much could missing pieces delay the process?
quests.explanation: 'Significantly' is a degree adverb modifying the verb 'delay', showing how serious the possible setback could be.
quests.grammarRule: Degree adverb modifying a verb

quests.question: Which part of speech does 'helpful' represent in this review?
quests.sentence: The staff were incredibly helpful, though the wait time was longer than expected, which was a bit disappointing.
quests.hint: Think about the job it performs here. What quality does 'helpful' give the staff?
quests.explanation: 'Helpful' is an adjective here, describing the staff's behavior, following the linking verb 'were'.
quests.grammarRule: Predicate adjective after a linking verb

quests.question: Staying with that review, which category describes 'though'?
quests.sentence: The staff were incredibly helpful, though the wait time was longer than expected, which was a bit disappointing.
quests.hint: This word introduces a contrast with the positive first half of the sentence. What contrast does it set up?
quests.explanation: 'Though' is a subordinating conjunction here, introducing a clause that contrasts with the praise given to the staff — the service was good, but the wait was long.
quests.grammarRule: Subordinating conjunction introducing a contrast clause

quests.question: In the same review, what role does 'which' play?
quests.sentence: The staff were incredibly helpful, though the wait time was longer than expected, which was a bit disappointing.
quests.hint: This word refers back to the entire situation of waiting longer than expected, not just one noun. What does 'which' refer to here?
quests.explanation: 'Which' is a relative pronoun referring back to the whole idea of the wait being longer than expected — the same whole-clause pattern seen several times earlier in this course.
quests.grammarRule: Relative pronoun referring to a whole clause

quests.question: Classify 'to confirm' as it appears in this voicemail.
quests.sentence: Hi, this is Dr. Alvarez's office calling to confirm your appointment tomorrow at three; please call back if you need to reschedule.
quests.hint: This 'to + verb' phrase explains why the office is calling, modifying the verb 'calling.' Why is the office calling?
quests.explanation: 'To confirm' is an infinitive functioning as an adverb here, showing the purpose of the call.
quests.grammarRule: Infinitive of purpose modifying a verb

quests.question: Which grammatical category fits 'to reschedule' in that same voicemail?
quests.sentence: Hi, this is Dr. Alvarez's office calling to confirm your appointment tomorrow at three; please call back if you need to reschedule.
quests.hint: This 'to + verb' phrase names what the listener might need, acting as the object of 'need.' What might the listener need to do?
quests.explanation: 'To reschedule' is an infinitive here, functioning as the object of 'need' — it names the action the listener might require.
quests.grammarRule: Infinitive functioning as a direct object

quests.question: Looking at the same voicemail, how is 'back' functioning?
quests.sentence: Hi, this is Dr. Alvarez's office calling to confirm your appointment tomorrow at three; please call back if you need to reschedule.
quests.hint: This word shows the direction of the return call. Which direction does 'back' point to?
quests.explanation: 'Back' functions as an adverb here, showing the direction of the requested call — a return call to the office. This is the same word seen earlier in this course as a noun (body part) and an adjective (back entrance).
quests.grammarRule: Direction adverb modifying a verb

quests.question: In this post, 'moved' is functioning as a:
quests.sentence: Just moved into the neighborhood and already loving the friendly vibe here!
quests.hint: In this casual post, the subject 'I' is left out. What did the poster do?
quests.explanation: 'Moved' is a verb here, describing the poster's action of relocating — short for 'I just moved'.
quests.grammarRule: Action verb in past tense (subject omitted)

quests.question: Within that same post, 'loving' is functioning as a:
quests.sentence: Just moved into the neighborhood and already loving the friendly vibe here!
quests.hint: This '-ing' word combines with an omitted 'am' to form the main verb. What is the poster doing right now, in an ongoing sense?
quests.explanation: 'Loving' functions as part of the verb here, short for 'I'm already loving' — the present progressive tense with the subject and 'am' omitted in this casual style.
quests.grammarRule: Verb in the present progressive tense (subject omitted)

quests.question: And in that same post, what part of speech is 'friendly'?
quests.sentence: Just moved into the neighborhood and already loving the friendly vibe here!
quests.hint: Remember that '-ly' words are not automatically adverbs. What quality does 'friendly' give the vibe?
quests.explanation: 'Friendly' is an adjective here, describing the neighborhood's atmosphere — the same '-ly' adjective pattern taught earlier in this course.
quests.grammarRule: Attributive adjective modifying a noun

quests.question: Which grammatical category best describes 'who' here?
quests.sentence: Employees who fail to submit timesheets by Friday will not be paid until the following cycle, regardless of the reason.
quests.hint: This word introduces a clause identifying which employees are meant. Which employees won't be paid on time?
quests.explanation: 'Who' is a relative pronoun introducing the clause 'who fail to submit timesheets by Friday', identifying which employees the policy affects.
quests.grammarRule: Relative pronoun introducing a descriptive clause

quests.question: Now consider 'to submit' in that same notice. What part of speech is it?
quests.sentence: Employees who fail to submit timesheets by Friday will not be paid until the following cycle, regardless of the reason.
quests.hint: This 'to + verb' phrase names what certain employees don't do, acting as the object of 'fail.' What do these employees fail to do?
quests.explanation: 'To submit' is an infinitive here, functioning as the object of 'fail' — it names the required action some employees don't complete.
quests.grammarRule: Infinitive functioning as a direct object

quests.question: In that same notice, what part of speech is 'regardless of'?
quests.sentence: Employees who fail to submit timesheets by Friday will not be paid until the following cycle, regardless of the reason.
quests.hint: This expression means 'no matter.' What doesn't change the outcome, according to the sentence?
quests.explanation: 'Regardless of' functions as a compound preposition here, introducing the phrase that shows the payment delay applies no matter the excuse.
quests.grammarRule: Compound preposition introducing an unaffected condition

quests.question: The word 'confusing' is being used as which grammatical category?
quests.sentence: Although the new policy seemed confusing at first, most employees adapted quickly, and productivity actually increased within the first month.
quests.hint: Look at what this word does in this exact sentence. What quality did the policy have at first?
quests.explanation: 'Confusing' is an adjective here, describing the policy's initial impression, following the linking verb 'seemed'.
quests.grammarRule: Predicate adjective after a linking verb

quests.question: Back in that same memo, what kind of word is 'adapted'?
quests.sentence: Although the new policy seemed confusing at first, most employees adapted quickly, and productivity actually increased within the first month.
quests.hint: Notice what the word is attached to. What action did they take?
quests.explanation: 'Adapted' is a verb here, describing the employees' action of adjusting to the new policy.
quests.grammarRule: Action verb in past tense

quests.question: And in that same memo, what part of speech is 'actually'?
quests.sentence: Although the new policy seemed confusing at first, most employees adapted quickly, and productivity actually increased within the first month.
quests.hint: Remember from an earlier lesson that this word can emphasize the truth of a statement. What does 'actually' emphasize here?
quests.explanation: 'Actually' is a sentence adverb here, emphasizing that productivity genuinely increased, despite the initial confusion — the same pattern seen in an earlier lesson about a manager closing early.
quests.grammarRule: Sentence adverb expressing emphasis

quests.question: How is 'to back up' functioning in this message?
quests.sentence: Please remember to back up your files before the system update tonight, since anything left unsaved could be lost, and IT will not be able to recover it afterward.
quests.hint: This 'to + verb' phrase names what the reader should remember, acting as the object of 'remember.' What should the reader remember to do?
quests.explanation: 'To back up' is an infinitive here, functioning as the object of 'remember' — it names the important task before the update.
quests.grammarRule: Infinitive functioning as a direct object

quests.question: In that same message, what part of speech is 'unsaved'?
quests.sentence: Please remember to back up your files before the system update tonight, since anything left unsaved could be lost, and IT will not be able to recover it afterward.
quests.hint: This word describes the condition of something left behind. What condition might files be in if not backed up?
quests.explanation: 'Unsaved' functions as an adjective here, describing the state of files that weren't saved before the update — similar to other participial adjectives like 'broken' or 'exhausted' from earlier lessons.
quests.grammarRule: Participial adjective modifying a noun

quests.question: Within that same message, 'afterward' is functioning as a:
quests.sentence: Please remember to back up your files before the system update tonight, since anything left unsaved could be lost, and IT will not be able to recover it afterward.
quests.hint: Set aside what you know about this word in general. When would IT be unable to recover the files?
quests.explanation: 'Afterward' is a time adverb modifying the verb phrase 'will not be able to recover', showing that the problem occurs after the update.
quests.grammarRule: Time adverb modifying a verb
